author: BBC News
description:
37 people have been killed after a huge explosion at an arms depot in Ukraine which was struck by a Russian drone.  The ams storage facility was based near a residential areas on the outskirts of the capital, Kyiv.  Hundreds of people have been evacuated from the area and a rescue operation is continuing, with fears that the death toll will rise.

Shells, mines and drones stored at the facility exploded in a massive blast that destroyed nearby homes nearby, including a care home for the elderly and disabled. 

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky strongly criticised the location of the depot near people’s homes, saying an investigation had been launched into "terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosive right next to people".

Russia's Ministry of Defence said that its forces had targeted "an ammunition depot”.

Ben Brown presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Dan Johnson in Kyiv.

author: BBC News
description:
Twenty-seven people have been killed and almost 400 evacuated after a Russian strike hit a warehouse near Kyiv, triggering a fire and a series of explosions.
 
Regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said a further 42 people, including four children, were injured after the Russian drone strike in the Bucha district.
 
An investigation has been launched into whether ammunition was being stored at the site, where search and rescue operations were ongoing early on Saturday.
 
Russia's Ministry of Defence said in a statement that its forces had targeted "an ammunition depot" in the Kyiv region village of Myla, which stores "components and launch boosters for FP-1/FP-2 long-range unmanned aerial vehicles".
 
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed his condolences to the families of the victims of the strike, saying that more than 300 emergency respondents had been deployed to the strike area.

author: BBC News
description:
More than 600 people have died following Wednesday's devastating flash flood in Nepal.
 
At least 2,426 people are missing, Nepal’s disaster management authority says, as rescue operations continue for a fourth day.
 
Families of the missing - including at least 517 foreign nationals - are waiting for news on the whereabouts of their loved ones.
 
Emergency teams are warning that rain is making it difficult to reach some of the worst-affected areas.
